Suiii. Cristiano Ronaldo is 41 and one of the most famous people to ever exist. Madeira kid, poor family, shared a room with his siblings. He left home for Lisbon at twelve. At fifteen he was diagnosed with a racing heart and had surgery that could have ended it before it started. Then Sporting, then United at eighteen, then Real Madrid, where he scored 450 goals in 438 games, which is absurd. Then Juventus, United again, and Al Nassr. Five Champions Leagues. Five Ballon d’Ors. Over 950 career goals and the most international goals in the history of the men’s game. What makes him different isn’t talent, it’s the obsession. He rebuilt himself physically three times to stay at the top as his body changed. Players half his age can’t match his data. The style is as controlled as everything else. Sharp tailoring, slim fits, all black or all white, serious watches. He’s been a fashion presence for twenty years and never looked scruffy once. Off the pitch he’s donated heavily and quietly to children’s hospitals and cancer care, funded a cancer centre in Portugal, paid for treatment for young fans, and he doesn’t have a single tattoo because he donates blood regularly.
